source.title: Arabic Safety Alignment as Selective Refusal: An Empirical Study of SFT, DPO, and Guard Calibration

page_placements.theme: Multilingual and prompt-framing transfer: harm separation and direction-based interventions weaken in non-English and low-resource languages

record.tranche_reason: The study extracts refusal directions and reports a qualitative direction-ablation result in which original refusals are preserved, which challenges the claim that ablating a single direction removes refusal. Its direction-score measurements do not establish causal mediation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports direction-score AUCs and calibrated direction-threshold operating points. These measure discrimination or threshold behavior, not the causal effect of removing or adding a direction. Table 28 reports qualitative direction-ablation outcomes but does not identify the models or give counts. SFT, DPO, and guard results are not included as rows because they do not apply, remove, add, or measure the claimed direction.
record.test_reason: The study extracts Arditi-style difference-in-means directions from Arabic prompts. It then uses them only as a harmful/benign score: AUC 0.909–0.956 and per-model threshold operating points (Table 26). These are discrimination results, not causal ablation or addition with refusal rates. The only ablation evidence (Table 28) is four redacted qualitative labels with no models, counts or rates. The wording is ambiguous: 'enabling ablated content' being redacted implies ablation produced enabling output, which is the opposite of the reader's reading. No version is tested in a way that can be scored.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but misweighted. The paper's central conclusion is that Arabic selective refusal is a model-specific operating-point selection problem across SFT, DPO and guards, and that MSA results do not ensure cross-script (Arabizi) reliability. The refusal-direction finding is a secondary remark: directions are detectable (AUC 0.909–0.956) but model-specific, so they support local calibration rather than a universal rule.
record.recipe_differences: The paper follows Arditi et al. to extract candidate directions across layers and token positions, then calibrates per-model thresholds on separate splits. It does not report a systematic causal ablation/addition test across every layer and position. The paper reports planned release materials but no public artifact URL.
record.method_sensitivity: Direction thresholds and score scales are model-specific; the paper calibrates thresholds separately for each model.

fits_no_version.finding: Difference-in-means refusal directions from translated Arabic prompts separate AraSafe harmful from benign prompts, AUC 0.909–0.956 across five models. Score scales and thresholds are model-specific.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A difference-in-means refusal direction is linearly readable in Arabic-language prompts across Arabic-centric and multilingual models, but needs per-model threshold calibration.

record.code_released: No public artifact URL is available in the current record; release is planned.
record.problems: The qualitative direction-ablation table does not identify models or provide example counts. The direction AUC and threshold-derived operating points do not by themselves demonstrate causal mediation. No general-capability preservation test is reported. Direction AUC uncertainty is described as a 95% half-width near 0.01, but the supplied table does not give per-model intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No other direction-related results left out. The paper's SFT, DPO, guard, cross-script refusal, judge-audit, and direction-threshold calibration details were not entered as claim rows unless they directly measured or applied the claimed direction.

untested.parts: Quantitative ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal, and capability preservation. The only ablation evidence is redacted qualitative labels.
No separation of harm judgment from refusal.
Directions are extracted and evaluated in Arabic. There is no test of transfer across languages, variants or base-to-instruct.
Directions are not re-extracted after SFT/DPO.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label rests on a misreading of the ambiguous Table 28 wording. With no counts or models, that table supports no verdict either way. The direction is used as a diagnostic classifier, so this is T4.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report a complete causal test of difference-in-means direction ablation at every layer and position, addition of the direction, or preservation of general capabilities. The qualitative ablation result lacks model identities and counts.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment is reported.
No attack is tested for suppressing the direction, and no training against its ablation is evaluated.
No comparison of one direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple directions is reported.
No test separates harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
The cross-script experiments evaluate selected SFT checkpoints, not transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or training stages.
The study compares training interventions on refusal rates but does not test whether training determines the existence of a removable refusal direction.

rows.check: The reader read 'Original refusal preserved; enabling content redacted' as ablation failing. Appendix E says the labels show the original refusal and that 'enabling ablated content' is omitted. That suggests the ablated output was enabling, i.e. refusal removed. No model, count or rate is given, so the outcome can't be read. The state should not be 'absent'.

labels.reason: No version is tested: AUC and threshold flag rates measure separation, not mediation. The directions are built and applied within Arabic, so V6 transfer is not tested. Rows R3-R12 rightly have versions none.

unmatched_labels.label: none
unmatched_labels.reason: No version is tested: AUC and threshold flag rates measure separation, not mediation. The directions are built and applied within Arabic, so V6 transfer is not tested. Rows R3-R12 rightly have versions none.

relation.reason: Directions are extracted on Arabic data and used as a detector for local calibration. The study does not test causal mediation (V1), cross-language transfer of one direction (V6), or harm-vs-refusal separation (V5).

tranche.reason: The study uses Arditi-style directions only as a harmful/benign score, reporting AUC and threshold operating points (Table 26, Figs 11-12). There is no ablation or addition with refusal rates. Table 28 gives only redacted qualitative ablation labels, with no rates or n.

source_check.notes: B/H in Table 26 are the rates at which the direction score flags benign/harmful AraSafe prompts (thresholds tuned on a separate 256+256 calibration split), not the model's refusal after an intervention. Table 28 lists redacted qualitative direction-ablation examples with no counts. The extracted fragment "testing their effect on refusal is important future work" (line 535) belongs to the related-work sentence on Arabic diacritics (Inoue et al.), not to the directions.

statements.correction: Extraction split: 1,000 benign Hala prompts + 1,000 translated BeaverTails harmful prompts, across layers and token positions (A.3). AraSafe AUCs 0.909-0.956 across five models, 95% half-width near 0.01 (Section 6; Table 26: 0.908965-0.955747). Score scales and thresholds differ by model.
statements.problem: Minor wording only. The text says the directions were computed 'Following Arditi et al. (2024)' and never says difference-in-means outright. Only the harmful half of the extraction split is stated to be translated.
